carousels.hook: Meta lookalikes work best with 300 engaged users
carousels.throughline: A small, engaged audience creates better Meta lookalikes than a large, cold one—here’s why and how to use it.

reel_beats.hook: Meta lookalikes work better with 300 engaged users than 30k cold ones

body.text: Meta’s lookalike tool needs people who already interact with your ads, not just a big list.
300 engaged users create a lookalike that costs 40% less per lead than 30k cold ones.
Engaged audiences mean Meta’s algorithm already knows who buys from you, so it targets better.
Cold lists include people who never saw your ad, so Meta has to guess who might like it.

chart.caption: Switching from a 30k cold list to 300 engaged users cut cost per lead by 40%.

carousels.throughline: Google Ads hides 20% of your buyers in the ‘Search terms’ report—here’s how to find and use them.

reel_beats.hook: Google Ads buries 20% of your buyers in a report you’ve never opened

body.text: Google Ads labels some buyers as ‘low intent’ even if they bought from you.
These buyers are hidden in the ‘Search terms’ report, not the main dashboard.
Most accounts never check this report—it’s buried under ‘Keywords’ in the menu.
Add these searches as new keywords—it can cut your cost per lead by 25%.

#MetaAdsTips #PaidSocial #AdCopy
carousels.hook: More budget burns cash on cold Meta audiences
carousels.throughline: Throwing more budget at a cold Meta audience won’t fix it—here’s the step-by-step fix that actually works.

reel_beats.hook: Throwing more budget at a cold Meta audience burns cash—here’s the fix

body.text: Step 1: Pause the cold audience—it costs €2 for every €1 that converts.
Step 2: Build a warm audience of people who visited your site in the last 30 days.
Step 3: Use a 3-part ad script—problem, solution, call to action—to re-engage them.
Step 4: Set a frequency cap of 2—don’t show the same ad more than twice a week.

screen.title: Which audience setting actually works
screen.mechanism: Warm audiences reach people who already know your business, not strangers.

Step 4: Set a frequency cap of 2—don’t show the same ad more than twice a week.
Step 5: After 7 days, check the ‘Engaged Shoppers’ report—these are your new buyers.
Step 6: Use that small, engaged audience to build a lookalike—it’ll cost 30% less per lead.

carousels.hook: Gmail’s spam filter ignores subject lines
carousels.throughline: Gmail’s spam filter skips subject lines and focuses on sender reputation—here’s how to use that to land in the inbox.

reel_beats.hook: Gmail’s spam filter ignores your subject line—it’s all about sender trust

body.text: Gmail checks your sender reputation first—subject lines come later.
High sender reputation means Gmail trusts your emails—even if the subject is weak.
Low sender reputation means Gmail buries your emails—even if the subject is strong.
Check your sender score at senderscore.org—above 80 is safe, below 70 is risky.
